sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: JAX kicker C.Little has made 22 [kc1] of 24 [kc2] field goals, a 91.7% [kc3] rate, but he is 66.7% [kc4] from 50-plus on 6 [kc5] tries, so treat a deep try in a close game as close to a coin flip. Punting is the bigger field-position lever: JAX nets 43.5 yards [kc8] on 32 [kc9] punts, but only 37.5% [kc10] are pinned inside the 20, so expect TEN to start many drives deep. JAX kickoff returns average 27.5 yards [kc13] on 37 [kc14] returns, and TEN's kick coverage allows 24.1 yards [kc15] on 33 [kc16] returns. Overall, JAX special-teams EPA ranks 8th [kc20] in the league.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: JAX's latest injury report lists two Outs: edge rusher BJ Green II and center Robert Hainsey. Hainsey has played 91.0% of snaps per game [ic3] over 9 games [ic4], so expect backup interior reps. Green's usage is too thin to read, at a 0.0% snap share [ic7] over 1 game [ic8]. Edge Danny Striggow and DT Matt Dickerson are Questionable. For TEN, guard Fernando Carmona is Out and receiver Carnell Tate is Questionable with a shoulder issue. Tate draws 18.7% of team targets [ic11] over 299 team targets [ic12], so his status matters most. Cornerback Micah Robinson and RB Tyjae Spears are also Questionable, but Spears carries only 10.4% of team rushes [ic15] over 212 team rushes [ic16].

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Four matchups should decide this game. First, JAX's passing offense posts 0.20 EPA per dropback [mc1] over 337 plays [mc2], ranked 3rd [mc3] in the league, against a TEN pass defense allowing 0.23 [mc4], 31st [mc5], with explosives on 10.9% of passes [mc6]. Keep the deep ball in front. Second, pressure: JAX's 31.6% blitz rate [mc9] meets TEN's 5.3% sack rate allowed [mc12], and Robert Hainsey, who has played 91.0% of snaps per game [mc13] over 9 games [mc14], is out, leaving JAX's interior protection thin. Third, the run: JAX stacks 6.9 defenders [mc15] and allows a 38.5% run success rate [mc16], while TEN's runs succeed 47.2% [mc17], so establish the run early. Fourth, kickoffs: JAX's return unit averages 27.5 yards [mc18] while TEN's coverage allows 24.1 yards [mc19], so placement matters.
